top_choice_rationale: P003 (Schultz, Chin, Wang; orthogonal translation systems and genetic code expansion) is a finished achievement: the concept was shown to work in living cells, was extended to multiple codons, orthogonal ribosomes and animals, and two decades of independent use, including as site-specific probes in enzymes like those I study, show the interpretation is stable. Its credit divides cleanly into three names and it asks the committee to settle no contested cut or approval question. P001 is the more novel mode of action and I rank it second, but it still needs a contested third name and a two-lineage citation while the clinical picture is moving. P002 is mature and cleanly attributed, but is a second member of a recognised cross-coupling family. Any award is preferable to none.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; Stockholm University colleague of Xiaodong Zou (not a candidate), and my respiratory-enzyme research could use genetic code expansion tools, but no documented tie to any proposed laureate
